note: Papers are those where an Aurora member is the first or second author, PLUS papers from Aurora-led JWST surveys (VENUS, led by S. Fujimoto; MINERVA, led by A. Muzzin), which are included regardless of author position and attributed to the survey lead. Recent items prioritize member-first-author papers. Authorship checked against the arXiv author list; 'venue' set only for papers confirmed published; dates follow the arXiv posting, or the journal publication when that is the news event. Links point to the ADS record. Do not add unverified papers, awards, figures, or venues.

items.title: Hidden mass in early galaxies revealed by bottom-heavy initial mass functions
items.blurb: Ultra-deep JWST/NIRSpec spectra of nine massive quiescent galaxies at z ≈ 0.7 reveal bottom-heavy stellar initial mass functions, an excess of low-mass stars that raises their inferred stellar masses.

items.title: VENUS: an ultra-faint galaxy hosting the metal-poor Type II supernova at z = 5.13
items.blurb: The first characterization of the host of the multiply imaged Type IIP supernova SN Eos at z = 5.13, where a total magnification of about 53 lets the team resolve the supernova's local environment inside an ultra-faint early galaxy.

items.title: Boötes III is a tidally disrupting ultra-faint dwarf galaxy on an eccentric polar orbit
items.blurb: Twenty-one member stars show that Boötes III is an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy being tidally disrupted on a highly eccentric polar orbit, caught about 0.14 Gyr after its latest pericentric passage.

items.title: Clues to inside-out quenching in quiescent galaxies at 1.2 ≲ z ≲ 2.2: age, Fe-, and Mg-abundances
items.blurb: Spatially resolved ages and abundances in eight massive quiescent galaxies at 1.2 ≲ z ≲ 2.2 show cores that are older, and possibly Mg-poor, compared to their outskirts, supporting inside-out quenching.

items.title: Light, heavy, primordial: exploring the diversity of black hole seeding and growth mechanisms in the JWST era
items.blurb: A unified comparison of light, heavy, and primordial black hole seeding and growth channels against the JWST census of early massive black holes, including the over-massive systems found in metal-poor hosts.

items.title: The THESAN-ZOOM project: Mystery N/O more – uncovering the origin of peculiar chemical abundances and a not-so-fundamental metallicity relation at 3 < z < 12
items.blurb: THESAN-ZOOM simulations show smoothly curved mass-metallicity relations already in place at z ≈ 12, governed by how well galaxies retain their metals, while the fundamental metallicity relation inverts for gas in low-mass galaxies.

items.title: First statistical study of over 100 magnified stellar events at z ≈ 0.72 with JWST
items.blurb: The first statistical sample of over 100 highly magnified individual stars at z ≈ 0.72, detected with JWST as microlensing transients near galaxy-cluster critical curves, opening a new probe of distant stellar populations and small-scale dark matter.

items.title: The kinematically hot, extremely metal-poor C-19 stellar stream in DESI DR2
items.blurb: Using DESI DR2 radial velocities and metallicities to characterize the C-19 stream, whose large velocity dispersion is hard to explain with a purely baryonic, disrupting globular-cluster progenitor.

items.title: The in situ growth of stellar-mass "light" seed black holes in nuclear star clusters
items.blurb: Magnetohydrodynamic simulations of how stellar-mass "light" seed black holes, the remnants of massive stars, form and grow inside nuclear star clusters as a possible channel toward supermassive black holes.

items.title: VENUS: a strong-lensing model of MACS J1931.8-2635 and the farthest multiply imaged supernova
items.blurb: A strong-lensing model of the cluster MACS J1931.8-2635 from the JWST VENUS survey, accompanying the spectroscopically confirmed supernova SN Eos at z = 5.13 and revealing new multiply imaged systems.

items.title: A new free-form lens model of AS1063 from ultra-deep GLIMPSE imaging
items.blurb: A new free-form lens model of the cluster AS1063 built from spectroscopically confirmed lensed galaxies and ultra-deep GLIMPSE imaging, which confirms and uncovers new lensed systems including a yellow-supergiant candidate at z ≈ 3.

items.title: VENUS: a multiply imaged Little Red Dot with an apparent blue component behind Abell 383
items.blurb: A doubly-imaged Little Red Dot candidate (A383-LRD1) behind the cluster Abell 383, showing an apparent blue component, from the JWST VENUS survey.

items.title: Black hole merger rates in the first billion years in light of JWST data
items.blurb: Modeling black-hole merger rates in the first billion years to test light- versus heavy-seed scenarios against the abundance of faint AGN that JWST finds at z = 4–9.

items.title: The ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST Survey: JWST/IFU optical observations of 18 main-sequence galaxies at z = 4–6
items.blurb: The ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST survey combines kpc-resolved HST, JWST, and ALMA imaging and spectroscopy of 18 main-sequence galaxies at z = 4–6 to resolve their stars, gas, and dust together.

items.title: The superclustering of hot gas: cosmological sensitivity in the WebSky simulations
items.blurb: Orientation-aware summary statistics of the superclustering of hot gas in the WebSky simulations, sharpening the cosmological sensitivity of thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich and galaxy cross-correlations.

items.title: The WebSky [CII] forecasts and the search for primordial intermittent non-Gaussianity
items.blurb: WebSky [CII] line-intensity mock maps that forecast upcoming wide-field submillimeter surveys (matched to CCAT) of cosmological [CII] emission from the epoch of reionization.

items.title: MINERVA: a NIRCam medium-band and MIRI imaging survey to unlock the hidden gems of the distant Universe
items.blurb: An overview of MINERVA, a JWST Cycle 4 treasury program of 8-band NIRCam medium-band and MIRI imaging across four CANDELS fields, designed to uncover distant and dust-obscured galaxies.

items.title: Quantitative morphology of Galactic cirrus in deep optical imaging
items.blurb: A morphological study of optical Galactic cirrus in deep imaging, using intensity statistics, angular power spectra, and wavelets to characterize the diffuse interstellar medium.

items.title: Synergising semi-analytical models and hydrodynamical simulations to interpret JWST data from the first billion years
items.blurb: Feeding cold-gas fractions and star-formation efficiencies from the SPHINX20 radiation-hydrodynamics simulation into the DELPHI semi-analytic model to explain the abundance of bright galaxies at z ≥ 11 and the drivers of reionization.

items.title: GLIMPSE: an ultra-faint Pop III galaxy candidate and first constraints on the Pop III UV luminosity function at z ≈ 6–7
items.blurb: A NIRCam-based search across ~500 arcmin² of JWST legacy fields turns up GLIMPSE-16043, a promising ultra-faint Population III galaxy candidate at z ≈ 6.5, and sets first limits on the Pop III UV luminosity function.
